name: Once.tools

sources.title: Once.tools homepage - 'Your guide to software you only have to pay for once', 172 tools across 14 categories
Submit a tool - simple open form (name, email, tool name, URL, tagline, description, price, video)

requirements: Niche directory: the site curates 'software you only have to pay for once' — a subscription-priced SaaS is a poor fit; a one-time-payment or lifetime-deal product is the intended submission
Submission is an open public form — no account or payment fields are shown
Listed across 14 categories (AI, Collaboration, Design, Developer Tools, E-Commerce, Form Builders, Marketing, Productivity, Screenshots, SEO, Social Media, Task Management, Video, Writing)
preparation: Tool name, URL, tagline, and description
Price field — prepare the one-time price (this directory's whole premise)
workflow: Go to https://once.tools/submit ('Submit' in the header)
Fill 'About the tool': name, URL, tagline, description, price, optional YouTube video
Submit the form — editorial review follows (no timeline published)
watchFor: Fit matters: the directory's premise is pay-once software — a monthly-subscription product may be declined or mislead the audience
No account system — updates presumably go through the same form or email
No published review timeline or notification promise
Small curated directory (~172 tools) — acceptance is selective, not a bulk-SEO play
countsAsLive: The tool appears in the once.tools grid and its category page with logo, name, and tagline
unknowns: Review timeline and whether approval/rejection is emailed
Whether the listing link is dofollow (catalog note says follow; unconfirmed)
Whether purely-free tools qualify alongside pay-once ones
